svg.title: The 1066 Crisis: Rival Invasions, Stamford Bridge & Battle of Hastings (Sept–Oct 1066)
svg.desc: KS3 Year 7 historical GIS atlas map of unpartitioned Britain and Ireland, the Kingdom of Norway, and the Duchy of Normandy in September–October 1066, showing Harald Hardrada’s 300-ship Viking fleet invasion to Fulford and Stamford Bridge, King Harold Godwinson’s 190-mile forced march north and 250-mile forced march back south via London, and Duke William of Normandy’s cross-Channel landing at Pevensey Bay and victory at Senlac Hill, Hastings.

g.text: Turning Points 1–4: Stamford Bridge to Senlac Hill

text.tspan: Channel winds turn; Duke William lands in Sussex unopposed
Exhausted Anglo-Saxon army races back south via London
Feigned retreats break shield wall; Harold slain

svg.text: KS3 HISTORY • YEAR 7 ENQUIRY: MEDIEVAL ENGLAND (1066–1381)
The 1066 Crisis: Rival Invasions, Stamford Bridge & Hastings
Fighting two invasions in three weeks—marching 190 miles north to Stamford Bridge and 250 miles south—exhausted Harold’s army.
On 14 October 1066 at Senlac Hill, Hastings, Duke William’s feigned cavalry retreats broke the Saxon shield wall and won the crown.
